proof:
Source: parent proof, T4 (integer multiplicity is local) together with (R), with the local hypothesis phrased through domain restrictions X|_B := X.restrictDomain (B ⊆ U), and the converse restriction statement used in Parts IV.3, V2 and V4(ii). The hypotheses (REP), (MR), (IMC) are the relevant parts of the frozen statements of the parent node's dependency theorems dimred_mbl_current_foundations (first conjunct), dor_imrep_massOn_eq_measure_and_support (mass identity) and dimred_mbl_current_foundations (second conjunct) (not available to this child otherwise, hence assumed); (IMC)(a)–(d) denote its four conjuncts. For an IMRep R = (M, θ, ξ) put R.measure := θHᵏ⌞M (contract IMRep.measure); then R.action(ω) = ∫_M θ ξ(ω) dHᵏ = ∫ ξ(ω) dR.measure (integral against a measure with density). ξ(ω) denotes x ↦ ξ(x)(ω(x)).

If U = ∅ then 𝒟^k(U) = {0}, X = 0 and both parts hold with the IMRep with empty carrier (mult 0, orient 0; all fields vacuous). Part (2) is the same statement as the accepted DAG declaration dtc_restrictDomain_isIntegerMultiplicity (not imported here; its argument is the one below).

Part (2) (restriction).
1. Let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an IMRep of X in U and V ⊆ U open. Since θ ≥ 1 on M, Hᵏ(M ∩ K) ≤ ∫_{M∩K} θ dHᵏ < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U.
2. Define R_V := (M ∩ V, θ, ξ). M ∩ V is Borel and ⊆ V; it is countably k-rectifiable as a subset of M (SimonGMT CountablyRectifiable.mono); θ is measurable and positive on M ∩ V; for compact K ⊆ V, ∫_{M∩V∩K} θ dHᵏ ≤ ∫_{M∩K} θ dHᵏ < ∞; ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for Hᵏ⌞(M ∩ V) (restriction of Hᵏ⌞M). Orientation: by (IMC)(a) in U with M ∩ V ⊆ M (both Borel, ⊆ U, local finiteness from step 1), for Hᵏ-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ V and every subspace Q, M ∩ V has approximate tangent space Q at x iff M does; together with the IMRep property of R this gives, for Hᵏ-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ V, a subspace Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k (M ∩ V) x Q and ξ(x) a unit orientation of Q.
3. For ω ∈ 𝒟^k(V) (also an element of 𝒟^k(U)), X|_V(ω) = X(ω) = ∫_M θ ξ(ω) dHᵏ = ∫_{M∩V} θ ξ(ω) dHᵏ, because ω(x) = 0 for x ∉ tsupport ω ⊆ V. So R_V represents X|_V, which is IM.

Part (1) (local implies global).
4. X has locally finite mass, so (REP) gives μ_X, ξ_X with μ_X(ℝ^P ∖ U) = 0, μ_X(K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U, μ_X(G) = M_G(X) for all open G, ξ_X μ_X-a.e. strongly measurable, |ξ_X(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for all x, α, and X(ω) = ∫ ξ_X(ω) dμ_X for ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U).
5. Local identification of measures. Fix x ∈ U, r > 0 with B_r(x) ⊆ U and an IMRep R_x = (M_x, θ_x, ξ_x) in B_r(x) of X|_{B_r(x)}. Put B' := B_{r/2}(x); its closure is a compact subset of B_r(x). For open G ⊆ B_r(x), the admissible forms for M_G(X) (forms in 𝒟^k(U), tsupport ⊆ G, pointwise norm ≤ 1) are exactly the admissible forms for M_G(X|_{B_r(x)}), with equal values; so M_G(X) = M_G(X|_{B_r(x)}) = R_x.measure(G) by (MR) applied in the open set B_r(x). Hence μ_X(G) = R_x.measure(G) for every open G ⊆ B_r(x). The measures μ_X⌞B' and R_x.measure⌞B' are finite (μ_X(B') ≤ μ_X(closure B') < ∞) and agree on all open sets (G ∩ B' is open ⊆ B_r(x)); open sets form a π-system generating the Borel sets, so μ_X⌞B' = R_x.measure⌞B' (Mathlib MeasureTheory.ext_of_generate_finite).
6. Local identification of orientations. Apply the sibling theorem dmcbr_setIntegral_eq_of_integral_eq (child restrict_unique) in the open set B' with (μ₁, ξ₁) := (μ_X, ξ_X), (μ₂, ξ₂) := (R_x.measure, ξ_x), (μ₃, ξ₃) := (0, 0): both measures are finite on compact subsets of B'; ξ_x is a.e. strongly measurable for R_x.measure ≪ Hᵏ⌞M_x; |ξ_x(y)(α)| ≤ |α| for R_x.measure-a.e. y by (IMC)(d); and for ω ∈ 𝒟^k(B'), ∫ ξ_X(ω) dμ_X = X(ω) = X|_{B_r(x)}(ω) = R_x.action(ω) = ∫ ξ_x(ω) dR_x.measure. Hence ∫_E ξ_X(ω) dμ_X = ∫_E ξ_x(ω) dR_x.measure for every Borel E and ω ∈ 𝒟^k(B'). Let ν := μ_X⌞B' = R_x.measure⌞B'. For a k-covector α, a compact K ⊆ B' and φ ∈ C_c^∞(B') with φ = 1 on K, taking ω := φα and E ⊆ K gives ∫_E (ξ_X(α) − ξ_x(α)) dν = 0 for all Borel E ⊆ K, so ξ_X(y)(α) = ξ_x(y)(α) for ν-a.e. y ∈ K. Exhausting B' by countably many compact sets and letting α run through a finite basis of k-covectors: ξ_X = ξ_x μ_X-a.e. on B'.
7. Gluing. U is second countable, so countably many balls B'_i := B_{r_i/2}(x_i) as in steps 5–6 cover U. Let A_i := B'_i ∖ ⋃_{l<i} B'_l (Borel, pairwise disjoint, ⋃_i A_i = U), and define M := ⋃_i (M_{x_i} ∩ A_i), θ(y) := θ_{x_i}(y) and ξ(y) := ξ_{x_i}(y) for y ∈ A_i, θ(y) := 0 and ξ(y) := 0 for y ∉ U.
8. IMRep fields. M is Borel and ⊆ U; M is countably k-rectifiable (each M_{x_i} ∩ A_i ⊆ M_{x_i}; SimonGMT CountablyRectifiable.mono and countablyRectifiable_iUnion); θ is Borel and ℕ-valued (countable measurable gluing) with θ ≥ 1 on M; for compact K ⊆ U, ∫_{M∩K} θ dHᵏ = Σ_i ∫_{M_{x_i}∩A_i∩K} θ_{x_i} dHᵏ = Σ_i R_{x_i}.measure(A_i ∩ K) = Σ_i μ_X(A_i ∩ K) = μ_X(K) < ∞ (step 5, A_i ⊆ B'_i); ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for Hᵏ⌞M because on each Borel piece M ∩ A_i it coincides with ξ_{x_i}, which is a.e. strongly measurable for Hᵏ⌞M_{x_i} (countable gluing of a.e. strongly measurable functions along a measurable partition). Orientation: fix i. For Hᵏ-a.e. y ∈ M_{x_i} there is Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k M_{x_i} y Q and ξ_{x_i}(y) a unit orientation of Q (IMRep R_{x_i}). Apply (IMC)(a) in the open set B_{r_i}(x_i) to M_{x_i} ∩ A_i ⊆ M_{x_i}, and in U to M_{x_i} ∩ A_i ⊆ M (local finiteness: θ ≥ 1 on M and on M_{x_i}, and ∫_{M∩K}θ, ∫_{M_{x_i}∩K}θ_{x_i} < ∞ for compact K in the respective open sets): for Hᵏ-a.e. y ∈ M ∩ A_i = M_{x_i} ∩ A_i the approximate tangent spaces of M_{x_i}, of M_{x_i} ∩ A_i and of M at y coincide. Hence for Hᵏ-a.e. y ∈ M, ξ(y) is a unit orientation of an approximate tangent space of M at y.
9. Representation. For ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U), using countable additivity of the (absolutely convergent) integral, μ_X(ℝ^P ∖ U) = 0, and steps 5–6 on A_i ⊆ B'_i:
   X(ω) = ∫ ξ_X(ω) dμ_X = Σ_i ∫_{A_i} ξ_X(ω) dμ_X = Σ_i ∫_{A_i} ξ_{x_i}(ω) dR_{x_i}.measure = Σ_i ∫_{M_{x_i}∩A_i} θ_{x_i} ξ_{x_i}(ω) dHᵏ = ∫_M θ ξ(ω) dHᵏ.
So (M, θ, ξ) is an IMRep in U representing X, and X is integer multiplicity. ∎
key_steps: (2): intersect the carrier of an IMRep with V; tangent spaces are unchanged a.e. by (IMC)(a); the representing integral is unchanged since test forms of V vanish off V.
(1): take the (REP) representation (μ_X, ξ_X) of X.
On each ball, masses of X and of the local IM current agree on open subsets, so μ_X = θ_xHᵏ⌞M_x there by (MR) and uniqueness of finite measures on open sets.
restrict_unique and coordinatewise testing give ξ_X = ξ_x μ_X-a.e. on the ball.
Glue the local IMReps along a countable disjoint Borel partition subordinate to countably many balls; check all IMRep fields ((IMC)(a) for tangent spaces).
The glued IMRep represents X by countable additivity of ∫ξ_X(ω)dμ_X.
